subject.title: [Feature]: Add global --dry-run mode to prevent all tool calls from executing

question: Should OpenClaw add a global agent tool-execution dry-run, and what exact paths must the guarantee cover before users can treat it as a safety boundary?
rationale: The request changes operator trust in tool execution and could be unsafe if any runtime path continues executing while the CLI reports a dry run.

options.title: Define and implement a full contract
options.body: Specify the guarantee across embedded, Gateway-backed, client, tool-search, and direct invoke paths before accepting a CLI flag.

options.title: Fold into broader safe modes
options.body: Track this under the broader Ask/Plan/Modify workflow if maintainers want a product-level mode system instead of a narrow dry-run flag.

options.title: Keep existing safeguards only
options.body: Decline the global preview guarantee and document sandboxing, approvals, and tool policy as the supported safety controls.

recommendation.title: Define and implement a full contract
recommendation.body: Specify the guarantee across embedded, Gateway-backed, client, tool-search, and direct invoke paths before accepting a CLI flag.

likelyOwner.reason: `steipete` has recent merged history on the adapter surface and is the strongest available routing candidate from current-main evidence.
